adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that a 3-character shortcut produces a 7-character context that fails validation. However, examining the diff shows: 1) The Javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but all actual implementations use 2-character shortcuts (e.g., 'ac', 'cc', 'rt', 'ci', 'dg', 'pg', 'te', 'ro', 'pc'). 2) The encoding format in encodeTokenId() concatenates sessionType.getShortcut() (2 chars) + tokenType.getShortcut() (2 chars) + grantShort (2 chars) = 6 chars total. 3) The SessionType and TokenType enums all have 2-character shortcuts ('on', 'of', 'tr', 'un', 'rt', 'lt'). The interface documentation saying '3-letters' appears to be a documentation error, but all actual implementations consistently use 2-character shortcuts, so the encoder/decoder works correctly. The finding misreads the actual implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33 — [P1 confidence 100] "String getShortcut();" Loading any existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the prior interface makes postInit invoke a missing abstract method and abort startup; the private-SPI rebuttal does not remove the concrete extension break, while keeping the mapping in the encoder would delete this method and all nine built-in overrides.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (line 33). This is a breaking change for any existing third-party implementations of this interface that were compiled against the previous version. When Keycloak starts and calls `postInit`, it iterates over all `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations and calls `getShortcut()` on each one. Any external implementation that doesn't have this method will cause an `AbstractMethodError` at runtime, breaking backward compatibility. While the interface is in `server-spi-private` (suggesting it's internal), the finding correctly identifies that this is a concrete breaking change for any existing extensions.

When a new grant type is deployed at runtime and getGrantTypeByShortcut() is called, the code blindly puts the new mapping into both maps without checking if the shortcut already exists. Looking at the diff, getTokenContextFromTokenId() in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java (lines 68-93) parses encoded token IDs and calls factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(gtShortcut) to resolve the grant type. adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the new `isAccessTokenId` matcher. Looking at the diff, the token ID format is `<6-char-prefix>:<uuid>` where the prefix is structured as sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantType(2). The code `items[0].substring(3, 5)` extracts characters at indices 3-4 (0-indexed), but the grant shortcut is at indices 4-5 (the last 2 characters of the 6-char prefix). This means the matcher will incorrectly accept tokens with wrong grant shortcuts and reject tokens with correct grant shortcuts.

adjudication.rationale: The test setup in `before()` manually populates `grantsByShortcuts` with only 'ro', 'cc', and 'na' shortcuts, but never calls `postInit()` which would set `sessionFactory`. The test `testIncorrectGrantType()` uses shortcut 'ac' which is not in the manually populated map. When `getGrantTypeByShortcut('ac')` is called, it returns null from the map, then tries to use `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream()` but `sessionFactory` is null, causing NPE.
